requirements.statement: Organize Email Tools around the existing component while preserving package identities, imports, behavior, licenses and independent use. Publish self-contained component ownership and source-backed requirements. Coordinate repository mapping without adding providers or application features.

acceptance.statement: Explain repository purpose, component map, retained layout, expansion boundaries and relocation impact using current repository names.
Retain historical requirement IDs, revisions and acceptance semantics, with public-safe provenance and protected original baselines and approvals.
Supply public agent guidance and component ownership; preserve runtime code and existing safety tests; verify fresh installed consumers.

requirements.rationale: Explicitly authorized documentation and organization of existing functionality.
requirements.failure_example: A consumer needs private context or assumes an unavailable capability is implemented.
requirements.plain_language: Email Tools contains the component that works today; its package names stay stable.
requirements.positive_example: A new caller installs the existing package and finds its component charter without private documentation.

requirements.statement: Provide complete public developer documentation of existing behavior, including installation, API contracts, caller configuration, authorization, transports, pagination, failures, recovery, lifecycle, extension and validation. Keep private data out; distribute through GitHub source/local builds only.

acceptance.statement: Provide a linked docs index and reading order, minimal and realistic runnable examples, exact offline expected output and supported runtime/language differences.
Verify documented signatures, imports, parameters, returns, error codes, limits and recovery against current source; document caller-owned live prerequisites without live writes or mail access.
Follow the public setup from a fresh checkout into a separate installed consumer; record validation and distinguish synthetic results from unobserved live behavior.
Document component-specific operations and extension boundaries required by the linked public documentation issue; preserve all accepted safety cases.

requirements.rationale: Explicitly authorized documentation and organization of existing functionality.
requirements.failure_example: A consumer needs private context or assumes an unavailable capability is implemented.
requirements.plain_language: A developer can install the library and integrate it using public instructions and credential-free examples.
requirements.positive_example: A separate consumer installs a locally built artifact, runs an offline success and failure path, and understands which responsibilities remain with the caller.

requirements.statement: Bind each caller-supplied opaque account handle to one already authorized Gmail service. Fail for an unbound handle without fallback.

acceptance.statement: Profile lookup using an unbound handle raises connector-owned authentication_required before accessing any service; no default or alternate account is used.
A bound opaque handle selects its supplied service for the read operations.

requirements.rationale: First durable owning capture of existing authorized extraction/release contract. Source and tests corroborate implementation; they are not user authority. No behavior or historical catalog is invented.
requirements.failure_example: A caller cannot use the connector independently or an unknown account silently reads another service.
requirements.plain_language: The caller names the account explicitly; a missing binding cannot read another account.
requirements.positive_example: A caller binds billing to its authorized service; profile(account="missing") fails before service access.

requirements.statement: Expose read-only profile lookup, caller-supplied message search with pagination, and full-message retrieval by ID. Preserve the existing read-only request shape and zero SDK retry setting.

acceptance.statement: Profile uses getProfile(userId="me"); search forwards caller query, page token and maximum results to messages.list(userId="me", q=..., pageToken=..., maxResults=...).
Message retrieval uses messages.get(userId="me", id=caller_message_id, format="full"); each profile/list/get request executes with num_retries=0.
Return the provider response dictionaries without application interpretation; the caller selects further pages and messages. No send, modify or delete operation is exposed.

requirements.rationale: First durable owning capture of existing authorized extraction/release contract. Source and tests corroborate implementation; they are not user authority. No behavior or historical catalog is invented.
requirements.failure_example: A caller cannot use the connector independently or an unknown account silently reads another service.
requirements.plain_language: The connector forwards three kinds of read request, and the caller chooses searches and pages.
requirements.positive_example: An invoice consumer supplies subject:invoice and a next-page token, then fetches a selected full message by ID.

requirements.statement: Define connector-owned errors. Keep Room Booking error translation at its compatibility boundary.

acceptance.statement: Export ConnectorFailure with a code; an unresolved account binding has authentication_required.
Room Booking translates applicable connector errors through its optional compatibility boundary; booking errors and interpretation are not dependencies of the standalone connector.

requirements.rationale: First durable owning capture of existing authorized extraction/release contract. Source and tests corroborate implementation; they are not user authority. No behavior or historical catalog is invented.
requirements.failure_example: A caller cannot use the connector independently or an unknown account silently reads another service.
requirements.plain_language: Generic account selection errors belong here; a booking caller translates them for its own domain.
requirements.positive_example: An unrelated consumer catches ConnectorFailure.code; a booking consumer receives its booking-specific translated error.

requirements.statement: The caller supplies an authorized Gmail service and owns credentials, refresh, queries, message interpretation, scheduling, delivery and application policy. Booking-specific recipient matching, receipt verification and reservation status remain in Room Booking.

acceptance.statement: The standalone connector creates no credentials, refresh owner, scheduler, delivery system or application policy; it uses the injected service and caller search inputs.
Exact tagged-recipient matching, receipt verification and reservation-state interpretation remain in Room Booking; standalone consumers can interpret unrelated synthetic mail.

requirements.failure_example: A caller cannot use the connector independently or an unknown account silently reads another service.
requirements.plain_language: Applications authorize and interpret mail; the connector only selects a service and reads.
requirements.positive_example: An invoice workflow owns its credentials and invoice rules while Room Booking separately owns reservation evidence.

requirements.statement: Provide an independently installable read-only Gmail connector with no Room Booking dependency. Room Booking adopts it optionally through a documented compatibility path.

acceptance.statement: Build and install the standalone distribution into a clean consumer without Room Booking and exercise a synthetic non-booking search/fetch workflow.
Exercise installed Room Booking with email absent and separately with the optional standalone connector installed, preserving existing callers.

requirements.plain_language: The Gmail component works by itself; booking callers may install it as an option.
requirements.positive_example: A clean invoice consumer installs only the Gmail wheel; separate booking consumers validate the optional integration.
